distractors.reason: 'Fluent' is an adjective, not an adverb. We say 'speak fluently', not 'speak fluent'.
'Fluency' is a noun meaning the ability to speak well. It cannot come directly after the verb 'speak' here.
'Fluid' describes liquids or smooth movement. We don't say 'speak fluidly' for language ability.

example_sentence: She can speak English very ___ after five years in London.
l1_interference: Polacy mogą użyć przymiotnika 'fluent' zamiast przysłówka 'fluently', bo w języku polskim słowa 'płynny' i 'płynnie' są blisko siebie. Pamiętaj, że po czasowniku w angielskim używamy przysłówka, np. 'speak fluently'.
explanation: In English, verbs are modified by adverbs, not adjectives. 'Fluently' tells us how someone speaks, so it follows the verb 'speak'.

related_collocations.example: Please listen carefully to the instructions.
She had to work hard to pass the exam.
I didn't sleep well last night because of the noise.

memory_tip: VERB + ADVERB: the adverb describes HOW the action happens (speak fluently, work hard); adjectives describe nouns (a fluent speaker).
